channel.title: Acme: W3C Changes
channel.description: Reports on substantive changes in W3C GitHub repositories.

item.title: WCAG Guidance Broadens Its View of Accidental Character-Key Shortcuts
item.description:
The Understanding document for WCAG 2.1.4 now explains accidental character-key shortcut activation as a concern for keyboard and screen-reader users as well as people using speech input. It retains the core advice that authors let users turn off, remap, or limit single-character shortcuts to the component that has focus.

The revision adds a key-event logger to help people discover which printable-key shortcuts a page exposes. This is informative WCAG guidance, not a change to the success criterion itself.

Changes: wcag commit 31c9b262.

item.title: SPARQL 1.2 Tightens the Formal Rules for Ordering and Expression Evaluation
item.description:
The SPARQL 1.2 query draft now uses a single ordering-condition model for ORDER BY, replacing overlapping comparator terminology and making the algebra easier to follow. It also explicitly defines evaluation of a variable as its RDF term when bound and as an error when unbound.

A related clarification enumerates the possible variable-or-term combinations in NPS evaluation. Together, the edits reduce ambiguity for implementers of sorting and path evaluation in the developing SPARQL 1.2 specification.

Changes: sparql-query commit b55ebb36; sparql-query commit 7f707ffe; sparql-query commit be19f51e.

item.title: W3C CSS Validator Adds Nesting and @scope Support
item.description:
The W3C CSS Validator can now parse nested rules, resolve nested selectors, and validate scoped style blocks. Its @scope handling also recognizes @keyframes and @font-face within a scope under the CSS Cascading Level 6 rules.

A follow-up fixes detection of custom properties nested inside calc(), avoiding false validation results when variables appear below the top level of a value. The changes make the validator useful for more modern CSS without treating these constructs as syntax errors.

Changes: css-validator commit 95ef4b6e; css-validator commit 8c452afe; css-validator commit f4cf8d53; css-validator commit 25ff4879.

item.title: RDF Test Suite Adds Edge Cases for GRAPH, VALUES, and Relative IRIs
item.description:
The W3C RDF test repository now covers several SPARQL graph-pattern edge cases: VALUES inside GRAPH when the graph variable is absent, nested GRAPH patterns, and LIMIT or OFFSET subqueries that must be evaluated separately for each named graph.

A further SPARQL 1.0 test checks relative-IRI resolution. These cases give query-engine implementers more precise interoperability checks around dataset scoping and base-IRI handling.

Changes: rdf-tests commit 5e5da96b; rdf-tests commit 8df7fc13; rdf-tests commit 047ddf97; rdf-tests commit ca72fa96.

item.title: MathML Full Drops Two Legacy Alignment Elements
item.description:
The MathML Full draft has removed malignmark and maligngroup, two legacy elements for decimal and marker-based alignment that were already absent from MathML Core. The document points authors who still need the behavior to a polyfill.

This narrows the larger MathML vocabulary around features with viable implementation paths. The edit affects the evolving MathML Full draft; it does not remove anything from MathML Core.

Changes: mathml commit 3ebba291.

item.title: ActivityPub Makes Public Outbox Responses a Normative Recommendation
item.description:
The ActivityPub specification now says a server SHOULD return all Public posts when an unauthenticated client requests an actor's outbox. The wording previously used a lowercase “should,” leaving its normative force unclear.

Capitalizing the RFC 2119 keyword makes the existing expectation explicit for server implementers while preserving it as a recommendation rather than an absolute requirement.

Changes: activitypub commit cca3043d.

item.title: EPUB 3.4 Marks the source-of Metadata Property as Outdated
item.description:
The EPUB 3.4 draft now lists the source-of metadata property among outdated features. Existing publications that use it remain conforming, but authors are no longer encouraged to rely on it for new content.

The change preserves compatibility while signalling where the format is moving. Reading systems still need to tolerate the property in older EPUB content.

Changes: epub-specs commit 358cb418.

item.title: SOSA/SSN Expands Its OGC API Alignment Guidance
item.description:
The SOSA/SSN draft now includes fuller alignment material for OGC SensorThings API and OGC API – Connected Systems. The new tables map navigation attributes, entities, resources, and inverse relationships to their SOSA/SSN counterparts.

The draft also restores supporting sections for common modeling patterns and profiles. This is guidance in an evolving ontology specification, intended to make translation between OGC APIs and SOSA/SSN data models more explicit.

Changes: sdw-sosa-ssn commit 5fcb3bd3; sdw-sosa-ssn commit 8111e32a; sdw-sosa-ssn commit 2a16b802.

item.title: MathML Clarifies Language Selection for Spoken and Braille Intent
item.description:
The MathML draft now says intent-based speech or braille output should use the nearest xml:lang value on the expression or an ancestor. If none exists, implementations fall back to the document language and then the system language.

The clarification gives assistive-technology and rendering implementations a deterministic language-selection order when interpreting mathematical intent.

Changes: mathml commit 10fb18bb.

item.title: Draft Linked Web Storage Charter Adds ODRL Coordination and a Delivery Timeline
item.description:
The draft Linked Web Storage Working Group charter now calls for coordination with the ODRL Community Group on using the ODRL information model in the protocol. It also replaces placeholder scheduling text with a proposed sequence for Working Draft, Candidate Recommendation, and Recommendation milestones.

Because this is a draft charter, the scope and dates remain proposals rather than approved commitments.

Changes: lws-wg-charter commit 82d38ba8; lws-wg-charter commit 67c033fb.

item.title: WebRTC Stats Removes totalEncodedBytesTarget
item.description:
The WebRTC Statistics draft has removed totalEncodedBytesTarget from outbound RTP statistics. The counter was meant to accumulate target frame sizes but did not have sufficient implementation support.

Implementers and telemetry consumers should no longer expect this member in the developing stats model; targetBitrate and the remaining encoding statistics are unaffected.

Changes: webrtc-stats commit eee09715.

item.title: DID Resolution Lets Extensions Define HTTP Status Mappings for New Errors
item.description:
The DID Resolution draft no longer requires every error type unknown to the core specification to map to HTTP 500. An external specification that defines an error may also define its HTTP status; otherwise the mapping is implementation-defined.

This gives extension specifications a way to distinguish client, authorization, and server failures without forcing unrelated errors into a generic internal-server response.

Changes: did-resolution commit a5f3d89f.

item.title: SHACL 1.2 Profiling Report States What Each Feature Must Demonstrate
item.description:
The SHACL 1.2 Profiling implementation report now describes the evidence expected for every feature, including profile declaration, imports, dependency checks, processors, validators, and profile-specific behavior.

The clearer criteria make implementation claims easier to compare and show what interoperability evidence will be needed as the profiling work advances.

Changes: data-shapes commit 976ed12a.

item.title: WebDriver Restricts Integer Values to JavaScript's Safe Range
item.description:
WebDriver now defines an Integer as a number within the inclusive JavaScript safe-integer range as well as unchanged by ToInteger. Cookie expiry validation consequently relies on that shared definition instead of repeating the upper-bound check.

The change prevents protocol values that cannot be represented exactly in JavaScript from being treated as valid integers and makes integer handling more consistent across commands.

Changes: webdriver commit 2adf7282.

item.title: SHACL-SPARQL Rules Refine Dependencies, Imports, and Execution Semantics
item.description:
The developing SHACL 1.2 SPARQL Rules language now gives more precise definitions for data dependencies, imports, and rule expressions. It also refines the stratification contract used to reason about sound execution and updates when run-once rules are evaluated.

Additional wording covers triple-term templates and related grammar. These changes are part of the draft rules language and are intended to make independent implementations agree on rule ordering and results.

Changes: data-shapes commit 4e9d3a08; data-shapes commit e74a8cb6.

item.title: YAML-LD Extended Profile Aligns with Stream Processing
item.description:
The YAML-LD Extended Profile draft now follows YAML-LD 1.0's stream model and removes duplicated definitions already supplied by the Basic Profile. Related tests update core-schema tag URIs and regenerate the manifest.

The change reduces overlap between profile layers and checks the revised behavior against the implementation-report test suite.

Changes: yaml-ld commit bbbde480; yaml-ld commit f13f7c7b.

item.title: EPUBCheck Turns Malformed Dates into Validation Errors Instead of Crashes
item.description:
EPUBCheck now handles a dc:date value ending in a bare decimal point as an invalid date rather than throwing an unhandled exception. Unexpected exceptions elsewhere are now reported as fatal RSC-016 errors and produce a non-clean exit status.

The result is more predictable command-line and API behavior: malformed books receive actionable validation output instead of appearing to terminate mysteriously.

Changes: epubcheck commit 0cc28fb2; epubcheck commit 33757363.

item.title: EPUBCheck Accepts Accessible Labels on Navigation Landmarks
item.description:
EPUBCheck's navigation-document schema now allows aria-label and aria-labelledby on nav elements. It also recognizes additional valid ARIA roles, including menu, menubar, none, presentation, and tablist.

This stops the validator from rejecting accessibility metadata that authors use to distinguish multiple navigation landmarks for assistive-technology users.

Changes: epubcheck commit 30f64e90.

item.title: AgendaBot Makes Encrypted Password Length Less Revealing
item.description:
AgendaBot now pads stored encrypted passwords with random bytes after a null delimiter instead of filling the remainder with predictable null bytes. Decryption stops at the delimiter and discards the random padding.

This does not replace the tool's existing masking design, but it reduces the amount of password-length information visible in the padded ciphertext.

Changes: AgendaBot commit 57326f78; AgendaBot commit f49b13c8.

item.title: CSS Color Preserves Chroma When LCH Hue Is Missing
item.description:
CSS Color 4 no longer converts an LCH or OKLCH color with a missing hue by zeroing both rectangular chroma components. The conversion now substitutes a hue of zero and computes a and b from the original chroma.

The previous algorithm discarded chroma and prevented accurate round-tripping between polar and rectangular color forms. The revision preserves more of the authored color state.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 9c50d377.

item.title: WebExtensions Public Suffix Proposal Rejects Leading-Dot Hostnames
item.description:
The proposed WebExtensions publicSuffix API now treats a hostname beginning with a dot as invalid instead of silently normalizing it. The proposal already rejected internal empty labels; the rule now covers the empty first label in values such as .example.net.

This remains a proposal rather than a finalized cross-browser API, but it gives extension authors and implementers a clearer input-validation contract.

Changes: webextensions commit 96f287b2.

item.title: Verifiable Credentials Clarifies When a Document Must Be Secured
item.description:
The Verifiable Credentials Data Model draft now distinguishes document conformance from securing a credential or presentation. A conforming VC or VP document is not inherently required to carry a securing mechanism, but when it is secured the mechanism must be one permitted by the specification.

The wording avoids treating every syntactically conforming document as already secured while retaining constraints on how security is applied.

Changes: vc-data-model commit 69ebe41c.

item.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Integrity Fixes Two Selective-Disclosure Algorithms
item.description:
The Verifiable Credentials Data Integrity draft corrects both the Salted Hash of Claims and Selectively Identified Claims procedures. The salted-hash flow now signs the correct list and limits salts to claims that are actually revealed; size and wording details are also tightened.

The selective-identification flow now filters signatures so a derived credential carries only those selected for disclosure. These changes affect draft algorithms used to minimize disclosed data.

Changes: vc-data-integrity commit 78e7e090; vc-data-integrity commit bb47d956.

item.title: Draft Agentic Web Charter Proposes WebMCP Standardization
item.description:
A new draft charter proposes an Agentic Web Working Group for standards that let AI agents interact with the Web on users' behalf. Its scope includes exposing site capabilities and context, representing agent identity and delegation, reporting interaction state, and expressing permissions or constraints.

The draft names WebMCP—JavaScript-based tools exposed by web applications to agents—as its initial normative specification. Model APIs, cryptographic primitives, crawler controls, content provenance, and bot detection are listed as out of scope. This is an early draft charter, not an approved group mandate.

Changes: charter-drafts commit cbe65854; charter-drafts commit 6e8619ec.

item.title: Accessibility Maturity Model Adds Evidence for Durable Governance
item.description:
The W3C Accessibility Maturity Model draft now asks organizations to show that accessibility governance can survive personnel changes. New proof points include tying sponsorship to a role rather than one person, documenting decision authority and reporting lines, naming backups, and defining vacancy procedures.

It also calls for retention metrics and records kept in organizational systems. The emphasis shifts maturity evidence from individual advocacy toward repeatable institutional practice.

Changes: maturity-model commit e275fbff.

item.title: SOSA/SSN Declares Missing Vocabulary Terms for OWL 2 DL
item.description:
The SOSA/SSN ontology modules now declare annotation vocabularies and other referenced terms needed for OWL 2 DL conformance. The patch also adds missing declarations such as Battery and preparedSample and repairs related imports and property use.

These changes matter to ontology processors: explicit declarations prevent profile violations and make reasoning behavior more predictable across the modular vocabulary.

Changes: sdw-sosa-ssn commit 6efa9434.

item.title: Payment Handler Removes the Obsolete Wildcard Origin Path
item.description:
The Web Payment Handler draft has removed algorithm text for a wildcard supported_origins value. The wildcard had already disappeared from the manifest format and from Chromium behavior, leaving the branch obsolete.

Payment handlers must therefore rely on explicit origin declarations under the current draft model rather than a catch-all marker.

Changes: web-based-payment-handler commit 3a498a6d.

item.title: Ask I18N Improves Keyboard Focus and Summarizes Active Settings
item.description:
The Ask I18N service now moves keyboard focus to the answer heading after a response is generated, making the result easier to reach without retracing the page. Its settings control also summarizes the active choices in localized text.

These interface changes make the question-and-answer tool clearer for keyboard and assistive-technology users while preserving the existing query workflow.

Changes: ask-i18n commit 6360a5f0.

item.title: ARIA Spinbutton Example Progressively Adopts ariaNotify
item.description:
The ARIA Authoring Practices quantity spinbutton example now uses ariaNotify when the browser exposes that method. On browsers without it, the example keeps its invisible live-region fallback for announcing value changes.

This is progressive enhancement in an example, not a normative ARIA requirement. It demonstrates how authors can adopt the newer notification API without dropping support for current assistive-technology combinations.

Changes: aria-practices commit 0f765e4d.

item.title: SHACL Rules Require a Stable NOW() Value Across a Rule Set
item.description:
The SHACL-SPARQL Rules draft now requires NOW() to return the same value throughout the evaluation of a rule set. Implementations cannot obtain a different timestamp for each rule or expression in the same run.

That matches the stable-query-time expectation familiar from SPARQL and prevents timing differences from changing which triples a rules execution produces.

Changes: data-shapes commit d556a1fc.

item.title: VC API Draft Adds Exchange-Specific Response Data
item.description:
The Verifiable Credentials API Lifecycle and Management draft adds ExchangeVerifiablePresentation and an exchangeData field. A response can now carry exchange-specific data that does not belong inside a verifiable credential, with a context definition and example showing the new shape.

This is draft API work. It gives protocol designers a typed place for transaction data without overloading the credential payload.

Changes: vcalm commit 922ad19d; vcalm commit 29b640ae; vcalm commit bdda148b.

item.title: WoT Thing Description Toolchain Eliminates Accepted Schema Failures
item.description:
The experimental Thing Description LinkML toolchain has closed its accepted-failure baseline: valid W3C examples must now pass the generated schema, and generated-versus-upstream mismatches fail tests directly. Fixes cover security-scheme dispatch, form variants, multilingual string maps, context arrays, and SHACL alternatives.

The repository is explicitly a temporary toolchain, so this is beta infrastructure rather than a change to the published Thing Description specification. It nevertheless raises the bar for generated artifact fidelity.

Changes: wot-thing-description-toolchain-tmp commit 9471ee73; wot-thing-description-toolchain-tmp commit f432e087.

item.title: CSS Adds a Wildcard Selector for Custom Highlights
item.description:
The CSS Custom Highlight API draft now defines ::highlight(*) to match every registered custom highlight whose name is a valid CSS identifier. The wildcard selector has zero specificity, letting more specific highlight rules override shared styling cleanly.

Names that are not valid CSS identifiers remain unmatchable, even by the wildcard. Authors can use the new selector for common highlight presentation without knowing every registered name in advance.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 568abd35.

item.title: Scribe Meeting Tool Adds a Command for Moving Transcript Lines
item.description:
W3C's Scribe meeting-transcript tool now supports a v// command that moves matching lines, complementing its existing substitution and editing commands. The parser also accepts text after a closing ]] link or fenced-code marker.

The additions give minute takers more control over reorganizing live transcripts without leaving the tool's command workflow.

Changes: scribe2 commit f0e90b0b.

item.title: VC Render Method Draft Dispatches Renderers by Suite
item.description:
The Verifiable Credential Render Method draft now dispatches rendering behavior through a renderSuite value rather than the generic type field. The associated data model is renamed SuiteRenderMethod, and presentation data formerly called card or data is consistently named summary.

The draft change separates the credential method's type from the concrete rendering suite, giving registries and implementations a clearer extension point.

Changes: vc-render-method commit bad7b72a; vc-render-method commit f366d67e; vc-render-method commit d00c2f11.

item.title: Reffy Recognizes HTML Elements Defined in Generic Definition Tables
item.description:
Reffy, W3C's specification-analysis tool, now recognizes HTML element definitions written in a generic dl.def table when the table identifies a DOM interface. This covers specifications such as HTML Ruby Extensions that do not use the usual dl.element class.

The filter still excludes unrelated definition tables, improving element and interface extraction without broad false positives.

Changes: reffy commit f2ada9e7.

item.title: CSS Scroll Snap Limits Capture and Alignment to the Relevant Scroll Container
item.description:
CSS Scroll Snap now says scroll-snap-type applies only to scroll containers and that snap positions are captured by the nearest ancestor scroll container on the containing-block chain. A single-axis scroller establishes snap positions only on its scrollable axis.

The draft also clarifies that scroll-snap-align resolves writing modes against the nearest relevant scroll container for each axis. Together, the changes remove ambiguous behavior around nested and single-axis scrollers.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit efada14c; csswg-drafts commit d603df84; csswg-drafts commit 528b2e31.

item.title: JSON-LD Guidance Favors Vetted Local Contexts for Predictable Processing
item.description:
The JSON-LD Best Practices draft now compares context-resolution policies and recommends that many systems use a vetted catalog of pre-downloaded contexts. The guidance explains how network fetching can introduce availability, mutability, spoofing, privacy, load, and latency risks.

It also discusses HTTP caching and cases where unknown contexts still need network access. The goal is an explicit resolution policy rather than assuming every context URI must be fetched live.

Changes: json-ld-bp commit 2d29b78d.

item.title: CBOR-LD Rejects Suffixes That Decode to the Wrong Structure
item.description:
The CBOR-LD draft now requires suffix decoding to fail with ERR_INVALID_PAYLOAD_STRUCTURE when the decoded value is not a map or array. Previously, malformed structural input could proceed without a dedicated check.

The explicit error gives decoders a consistent failure mode before they try to apply CBOR-LD processing rules to an incompatible payload.

Changes: cbor-ld commit 8c2301d2.

item.title: WCAG2ICT Draft Adds AAA and European-Standard Comparisons
item.description:
The WCAG2ICT draft now explains how its update differs from the 2025 Group Note, including newly incorporated Level AAA guidance. It also updates the mapping to EN 301 549 version 4.1.1 for applying WCAG success criteria to non-web documents and software.

These comparison sections are informative aids for policy and procurement users. The document remains draft guidance for applying WCAG outside web content.

Changes: wcag2ict commit 2cd5d3cc; wcag2ict commit 283e85e3.

item.title: Recognized Entities Draft Generates Security and Privacy Considerations from Threats
item.description:
The Recognized Entities draft now builds its security, privacy, and market-competition considerations from a structured threat model. The main document gains sections that summarize identified threats and link back to the separate model.

This brings the risks into the specification developers are most likely to read while keeping the detailed threat records in one place. The change concerns an evolving draft and its publication process; it does not declare the threat model complete.

Changes: vc-recognized-entities commit 2ab49aac.

item.title: Verifiable Credentials Draft Connects Security Guidance to Its Threat Model
item.description:
The Verifiable Credentials Data Model draft now generates parts of its security and privacy considerations from the project's structured threat model. The change adds a rendering step that brings threat summaries into the main specification.

That creates a more direct path from identified risks to the guidance implementers read. It also reduces the chance that the separate threat model and the main document drift apart as threats are revised. Supporting publication changes this week prepared the threat model as a W3C Draft Note; the generated sections do not by themselves change the protocol.

Changes: vc-data-model commit 15311632.

item.title: DID Extensions Registry Deprecates Four Stale Resolution Errors
item.description:
The DID Extensions registry has marked four error entries as deprecated after their definitions were removed from the DID Resolution draft in January 2026. The entries remain visible, but now point readers to the older Working Draft that defined them.

This preserves a record for implementations that may still encounter the names while making clear that current DID Resolution work no longer defines them. The change affects the registry's status and references; it does not itself change DID resolution behavior.

Changes: did-extensions commit 8d802b2a.

item.title: W3C Publishing Tool Adds a Static-HTML Route
item.description:
W3C's spec-prod publishing tool now accepts TOOLCHAIN: static for a source document that is already built as publishable HTML. In this mode it copies the document without running ReSpec or Bikeshed.

The rest of the publication pipeline still validates the output, copies relevant assets, and deploys it. That gives editors a supported route for specifications produced by other build systems, or for documents whose final HTML should be published as-is.

Changes: spec-prod commit ef658223.

item.title: W3C String Search Draft Adds Internationalization Best Practices
item.description:
The W3C String Search draft has added concrete best practices for search sensitivity. It recommends case-insensitive matching by default using Unicode full case folding, while letting users request more exact matches, including case- and diacritic-sensitive search.

The new guidance also treats width variants as equivalent by default and distinguishes a search term with diacritics from one without them. It advises interfaces to reward more precise user input with more selective results. These are recommendations in a draft, aimed at making search work better across languages and scripts.

Changes: string-search commit 7b861f9d.

item.title: WebAuthn Explores Passkey Sign-In Without a Login Form
item.description:
A revised WebAuthn explainer proposes a way for sites to offer passkey sign-in on pages that have no login form. A site would make a conditional credentials request with uiMode set to passive, allowing the browser to show eligible credentials in a small, dedicated prompt.

The proposal is aimed at cases such as opening an article or storefront while signed out. If no eligible credential exists, the browser would show no prompt and the request would remain pending. The explainer also discusses showing passwords or FedCM credentials in the same browser surface. This is an explainer, not a change to the WebAuthn specification.

Changes: webauthn commit 21d32d45.

item.title: SOSA Corrects an Inverse Property in Its Sensor Ontology
item.description:
The SOSA sensor and observation ontology now identifies sosa:isUltimateFeatureOfInterestOf as the inverse of sosa:hasUltimateFeatureOfInterest. The RDF vocabulary gains the matching owl:inverseOf statement.

Related fixes correct a namespace in a battery-lifetime example and use the proper property for prepared samples in an ontology extension. These are small edits with real consequences for software that reads the RDF: an incorrect inverse or property URI can produce wrong inferences.

Changes: sdw-sosa-ssn commit b2db42b2; sdw-sosa-ssn commit 38f631f1.

item.title: CSS View Timelines Now Require a Subject
item.description:
The CSS Scroll-driven Animations draft now requires a subject when a script constructs a ViewTimeline. The ViewTimelineOptions dictionary marks subject as required, and the constructor no longer accepts an omitted options object.

A view timeline measures progress as an element moves through a scrollport. Without a subject element, that calculation has no meaningful target. The change makes the Web IDL match that dependency and gives implementers a clear basis for rejecting a constructor call that omits it.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit d1232f97.

item.title: EPUB Annotations Adds Detailed Security Guidance
item.description:
The developing EPUB Annotations specification now has a substantial security section instead of a placeholder.

The new guidance starts from the assumption that imported annotations can be hostile. Reading systems are told to treat detached files and annotations obtained from external servers as untrusted input.

The section addresses script injection, unsafe URI schemes, automatic loading of external resources, path traversal outside an EPUB container, denial-of-service risks from complex selectors or large data structures, and forged creator information.

It also reinforces an important design decision: annotation bodies are plain text. Reading systems must not interpret embedded HTML or script markup as executable content. For imported annotations, creator metadata alone is not proof of who created them.

Changes: epub-specs commit bbd1bf2f.

item.title: EPUB Annotation Data Model Gets Simpler and More Specific
item.description:
Several changes this week tightened the developing EPUB Annotations data model.

One removed the unfinished Meta object, limited annotation targets to EPUB top-level content documents and simplified the metadata used to associate an annotation set with a publication.

A later revision removed commenting as an explicit annotation motivation, leaving bookmarking and highlighting. A note or comment can instead be the body of either a bookmark or highlight.

That revision also specifies that a missing motivation is treated as a bookmark and clarifies how selectors should distinguish a point-like bookmark from a highlighted range.

These are still changes to a developing specification, but they narrow the model implementers are being asked to support.

Changes: epub-specs commit 763f7b30; epub-specs commit e6dd274a.
